column1: Between 1908 and 1924, Gwendoline and Margaret Davies amassed one of the largest collections of late-nineteenth and early-twentieth-century French paintings in Britain
column2: 1908年至1924年间，格温多琳与玛格丽特·戴维斯收藏了一批19世纪晚期至20世纪早期的法国画作，规模位居英国同类收藏前列。
column4: one of the largest|规模最大者之一

column1: Gwendoline (1882-1951) and Margaret (1884-1963) Davies were the granddaughters of David Davies, a Welshman who amassed a fortune in the shipping and mining industries.
column2: 格温多琳·戴维斯（1882—1951）和玛格丽特·戴维斯（1884—1963）是戴维·戴维斯的孙女。她们的祖父是威尔士人，凭借航运业和采矿业积累了巨额财富。
column5: amassed a fortune|积累巨额财富

column1: In 1907, when Gwendoline came into her inheritance (Margaret would follow in 1909), the sisters were said to be the wealthiest unmarried women in Britain.
column2: 1907年，格温多琳继承遗产，当时据说这对姐妹是全英国最富有的未婚女性。玛格丽特则要到1909年才继承遗产。
column3: came into her inheritance|继承遗产

column1: Their religious upbringing in rural Wales gave them a deep sense of social responsibility and they chose to use their inheritance for cultural and philanthropic* purposes.
column2: 姐妹俩在威尔士乡村受到的宗教教养赋予了她们强烈的社会责任感，她们决定把继承的财富用于文化和慈善事业。
column5: a deep sense of|强烈的……意识

column1: While there was no real family history of art collecting, the sisters' education was rigorously geared toward such pursuits.
column2: 这个家庭虽然并没有什么收藏艺术品的传统，但姐妹俩所受的教育却很有针对性，正是朝这类兴趣活动来培养她们的。
column3: family history|家族传统；家族历史
column8: pursuits|n. 所从事或追求的活动

column1: Their London school focused on cultural rather than academic study, and they travelled extensively with their governess, Jane Blaker, visiting art galleries and making extensive notes on the collections there.
column2: 她们在伦敦就读的学校更看重文化修养，学术研习则居于其次。她们还随家庭女教师简·布莱克四处旅行，参观美术馆，并为馆中藏品作了大量笔记。

column1: The sisters began to make regular art purchases from 1908, which roughly coincided with the dates of their inheritance.
column2: 姐妹俩从1908年开始定期购买艺术品，大致就在两人先后继承遗产的那几年。

column1: They took advice from various people, including the art dealer Hugh Blaker (the brother of Jane Blaker) and David Croal Thompson, who was also an art dealer.
column2: 她们向多方征求意见，其中包括艺术品经销商休·布莱克（简·布莱克的兄弟），以及同为艺术品经销商的戴维·克罗尔·汤普森。

column1: While it was long assumed that these men were largely responsible for the nature of the sisters' collection, it has recently been accepted that Gwendoline and Margaret retained a far more active role in the process.
column2: 长期以来，人们以为主要是这两位经销商决定了姐妹俩收藏什么样的作品；近来人们才认可，其实格温多琳和玛格丽特自己在收藏过程中发挥了积极得多的作用。

column1: The sisters' journals reveal their preference for Old Master** paintings.
column2: 从姐妹俩的日记可以看出，她们偏爱欧洲古典大师的画作。
column6: Old Master|欧洲古典艺术大师

column1: Yet they initially made very few attempts to secure any such works.
column2: 然而起初，她们很少尝试把这类作品买下来。

column1: While the sisters were wealthy in relative terms, their income was nothing compared to the fortunes of American art collectors of this period, such as J. Pierpont Morgan.
column2: 姐妹俩尽管相对富裕，但她们的收入同这一时期美国艺术品收藏家的巨额财富相比，根本不值一提，皮尔庞特·摩根就是这样一位美国收藏家。
column6: was nothing compared to|与……相比算不了什么

column1: Quite simply, high quality Old Master works were, if not beyond their means, then beyond what they were willing to pay for them.
column2: 说得直白些，品质上乘的古典大师画作，即使姐妹俩付得起，价格也超过了她们愿意出的数目。
column5: Old Master|欧洲古典艺术大师
column6: beyond their means|超出她们的经济能力

column1: Instead, their early purchases were of the fashionable, safe variety, and included, for example, paintings by the French artist Jean-Baptiste-Camille Corot.
column2: 她们早期买的反而是时兴、稳妥的那一类作品，其中就有法国画家让-巴蒂斯特-卡米耶·柯罗的画。

column1: However, it was only a few years before their collecting took a new direction and they turned to the work of the French Impressionists***.
column2: 不过，只过了几年，她们的收藏方向就发生了变化，转向了法国印象派画家的作品。
column3: only a few years|仅仅几年
column5: took a new direction|转向新的方向

column1: We know that Hugh Blaker, as a champion of contemporary French art had a hand in the decision, and we know also that they would have seen examples on their various trips to Paris.
column2: 我们知道，当代法国艺术的拥护者休·布莱克参与促成了这一决定；我们也知道，姐妹俩在数次巴黎之行中想必见过这类作品。
column5: had a hand in|参与促成

column1: Whatever the precise reason for this change, their first purchases of Impressionist art, made in October 1912, were scenes of Venice by the French artist Claude Monet.
column2: 无论这次转变的确切原因是什么，她们首次购入的印象派作品都是法国画家克洛德·莫奈描绘威尼斯景色的画作，购于1912年10月。

column1: Over the next 12 years, the sisters amassed the bulk of their Impressionist collection, including six further works by Monet, two more by Manet, and three by Renoir, including his well-known painting La Parisienne.
column2: 在接下来的12年里，姐妹俩购入了她们印象派藏品中的大部分，其中还有六幅莫奈的画、两幅马奈的画和三幅雷诺阿的画，后者包括名作《巴黎女郎》。

column1: The First World War (1914-1918) played a part in the development of the sisters' collection.
column2: 第一次世界大战（1914—1918）在姐妹俩收藏的发展过程中也起了作用。
column3: First World War|第一次世界大战
column4: played a part in|在……中起作用

column1: Their initial response to the war effort was to finance the safe passage of artists from occupied Belgium to Wales, as a humanitarian act, but also with the hope of establishing a vibrant artists' community in the area.
column2: 战争初起，姐妹俩出资让艺术家从被占领的比利时安全前往威尔士；这既是出于人道考虑，她们也希望在当地建立一个充满活力的艺术家群体。
column9: with the hope of|怀着……的希望

column1: Later in the conflict, both sisters decided to volunteer at a canteen for troops at Troyes, in northern France; Gwendoline in 1916, followed by Margaret in 1917.
column2: 战事持续期间，姐妹俩后来都决定去法国北部特鲁瓦的一家军人食堂当志愿者。格温多琳于1916年前往，玛格丽特则于1917年跟随她的脚步。

column1: It was tedious and distressing work, which would have a permanent effect on Gwendoline's health.
column2: 这份工作单调乏味，也让人痛心，给格温多琳的健康留下了永久影响。

column1: Yet on one of numerous trips to nearby Paris, she visited the Bernheim-Jeune Gallery.
column2: 不过，在多次前往附近巴黎的旅程中，有一次她去了贝尔内姆-热纳画廊。

column1: Here she acquired two works by Cézanne – Provençal Landscape and The François Zola Dam.
column2: 她在这里买下了两幅塞尚的作品——《普罗旺斯风景》和《弗朗索瓦·左拉水坝》。

column1: The paintings were shipped directly to Bath, England, where they became the first works by Cézanne to go on display in a public gallery in Britain.
column2: 这两幅画被直接运到英格兰的巴斯，成为英国第一批在公共美术馆展出的塞尚作品。

column1: Commentators have often described the sisters as unlikely pioneer collectors.
column2: 评论者常说，很难想到这对姐妹会成为开先河的收藏家。

column1: Much is made of their isolation in rural Wales and the fact that they didn't make friends with artists or gallery owners.
column2: 人们常拿两件事大做文章：她们远居威尔士乡间，而且同艺术家或画廊老板没有私交。
column3: Much is made of|人们格外强调
column4: isolation|n. 与外界隔绝的状态

column1: Yet they didn't feel obliged to follow fashionable tastes and were free to pursue their own preferences.
column2: 然而，她们并不觉得自己有义务追随流行品味，尽可以按自己的喜好收藏。

column1: Although they relied on a trusted circle of advisers, they made frequent trips to London and Paris, and also regularly had paintings sent to their home for consideration.
column2: 虽然她们倚重一群信任的顾问，却也经常亲自去伦敦和巴黎，还常让人把画送到家里，供自己挑选斟酌。

column1: By the early 1920s, Gwendoline felt increasingly uncomfortable buying art works when faced with the poverty and social upheaval created by the First World War.
column2: 到了20世纪20年代初，面对一战造成的贫困和社会动荡，格温多琳在购买艺术品时越发感到不安。

column1: Her philanthropic pursuits then became focused almost exclusively on social causes and the development of the sisters' home at Gregynog Hall into a conference center and venue for the Gregynog Festival of Music and Poetry.
column2: 此后，她几乎将全部慈善精力用于社会公益事业，以及改建姐妹俩的住所格雷吉诺格庄园，把这里建成会议中心和格雷吉诺格音乐与诗歌节的举办场地。

column1: Gwendoline made her final art purchase in March 1926.
column2: 格温多琳最后一次购藏艺术品是在1926年3月。

column1: Margaret also stopped collecting around this time, but started again in the 1930s acquiring, on a relatively small scale, work by contemporary British artists.
column2: 玛格丽特也在这段时期暂停收藏，但在20世纪30年代又开始购买当代英国艺术家的作品，只是规模相对较小。
column5: around this time|大约在这个时候
column7: on a relatively small scale|以相对较小的规模

column1: The sisters collected French Impressionist paintings at a time when such art was routinely ignored by individuals and institutions alike.
column2: 姐妹俩收藏法国印象派绘画时，无论个人还是机构，通常都对这类艺术漠不关心。
column5: at a time when|在……的时期

column1: The Gwendoline and Margaret Davies collection, donated in 1951 and 1963 respectively to the National Museum Wales, contains major examples of work by leading French Impressionists.
column2: 格温多琳和玛格丽特·戴维斯的收藏分别于1951年和1963年捐给威尔士国家博物馆，其中有多位法国印象派名家的重要代表作。

column1: In collecting paintings that they loved, the sisters created a lasting and meaningful cultural legacy for the people of Wales and beyond.
column2: 姐妹俩收藏自己喜爱的画作，为威尔士乃至更广地区的人们留下了一份意义深远、经久不衰的文化遗产。
